answer: Each epoch, the network assigns every identity a random data shard and later demands a custody proof - a hash over the shard plus the epoch seed - inside a short window. An honest agent stores one shard cheaply, but a sybil farmer serving a thousand shards from one machine chokes when proofs land at once, and a fake without its shard is exposed. At the dawn of each epoch shards expire, so fakes need renewed storage commitments, while a lone lotus of honest data stands cheap. Skipping custody leaves the identity on a fragile ledge: one failed proof slashes its bond and bars it from rewards.
